assistant_messages.content:
The diagram below shows how a supplier invoice moves from receipt to payment, based on your **Invoice Approval Policy** from Finance Operations. Every invoice follows the same steps in the same order. Note that this file calls itself a generated test document with no real suppliers, people or amounts [2], so check that it matches your live policy.

**The main steps:**
- **Matching check:** Accounts payable logs the invoice on the day it arrives. It then checks the invoice against the purchase order and the goods receipt note: same supplier, same quantities, same unit prices [2].
- **If it doesn't match:** The invoice is sent back to the supplier with the reason. The supplier fixes it and sends it again, and it goes through the matching check once more. A rejected invoice is never paid [1].
- **Approvals:** The budget holder for the cost centre has five working days to approve. Invoices over €10,000 also need the finance controller's sign-off after that [1].
- **Payment and filing:** Payments go out in the weekly run on Thursdays [3]. The paid invoice, its purchase order and its approvals are then kept in the audit archive for seven years [3].

**Other rules not shown in the diagram:**
- **Order of approvers:** Accounts payable clerk, then budget holder, then finance controller (only over €10,000), then treasury, which releases the payment [4].
- **No self-approval:** Nobody may approve an invoice they raised [4].
- **Late approvals:** If the budget holder hasn't approved within five working days, accounts payable sends a reminder. After a second reminder, the invoice goes to the head of finance [4].

The diagram below shows how a supplier invoice moves from receipt to payment, based on your **Invoice Approval Policy** from Finance Operations. Every invoice follows the same steps in the same order. Note that this file calls itself a generated test document with no real suppliers, people or amounts [2], so check that it matches your live policy.

**The main steps:**
- **Matching check:** Accounts payable logs the invoice on the day it arrives. It then checks the invoice against the purchase order and the goods receipt note: same supplier, same quantities, same unit prices [2].
- **If it doesn't match:** The invoice is sent back to the supplier with the reason. The supplier fixes it and sends it again, and it goes through the matching check once more. A rejected invoice is never paid [1].
- **Approvals:** The budget holder for the cost centre has five working days to approve. Invoices over €10,000 also need the finance controller's sign-off after that [1].
- **Payment and filing:** Payments go out in the weekly run on Thursdays [3]. The paid invoice, its purchase order and its approvals are then kept in the audit archive for seven years [3].

**Other rules not shown in the diagram:**
- **Order of approvers:** Accounts payable clerk, then budget holder, then finance controller (only over €10,000), then treasury, which releases the payment [4].
- **No self-approval:** Nobody may approve an invoice they raised [4].
- **Late approvals:** If the budget holder hasn't approved within five working days, accounts payable sends a reminder. After a second reminder, the invoice goes to the head of finance [4].
